 1                  I.     WITNESS IDENTIFICATION AND QUALIFICATIONS

 2   Q.      Please state your name and business address.

 3   A.      My name is Michele A. Kietzman. My business address is 401 Nicollet Mall,

 1          II.      BENCH REQUEST QUESTIONS ADDRESSED IN THIS
 2                           SUPPLEMENTAL TESTIMONY

 3                              QUESTION NO. NMPRC 1-(m):

4    Q.   Please provide a list of Rule 440 Reports, filed since SPS's last rate case, that

5         are included in the Application, along with the associated costs. For each cost,

6         indicate whether it relates to generation, transmission, distribution facilities,

7         or a combination of these categories.

 8   A.   Please refer to Attachment MAK-BR-1(m), tab ‘Filed 440s’, which lists the Rule

 9        440 reports filed since SPS’s last rate case that are reflected in the Application, the

10        associated costs, and whether those costs relate to generation, transmission, or

11        distribution facilities.

12                As a member of the capital asset accounting group, I do not sponsor the

13        need for, or development of, the individual projects reflected in Attachment MAK-

14        BR-1(m). My group, which is responsible for all aspects of fixed-asset accounting,

15        compiles the accounting data for SPS’s capital projects and provides that

16        aggregated information to witnesses responsible for sponsoring capital additions

17        within their respective business areas, including generation, transmission, and

18        distribution. Those business area witnesses explain the need for the projects and




                                                3
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Supplemental Testimony
                                              of
                                     Michele A. Kietzman

 1        the analyses and review processes used to ensure that the project expenditures are

 2        reasonable and necessary.

 3               The plant amounts contained in my pre-filed direct testimony build on the

 4        actual or forecasted capital expenditure data that the individual business areas

 5        provide. After the business area witnesses determine the capital investment

 6        amounts, my department calculates the associated plant balances and expenses,

 7        including Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (“AFUDC”),

 8        depreciation expense, and deferred income taxes. SPS is providing Attachment

 9        MAK-BR-1(m) for ease of reference for the Commission.

10   Q.   Are you responsible for preparing or filing Rule 440 reports on behalf of SPS?

11   A.   No. I am not responsible for preparing or filing Rule 440 reports. My role at SPS

12        centers on fixed-asset accounting. In that capacity, my department records capital

13        expenditures associated with SPS’s capital projects and calculates the resulting

14        plant balances and related expenses reflected in this case.

15   Q.   Are you a subject matter expert on the requirements or filing mechanics of

16        Rule 440?

17   A.   No. I am not a subject matter expert on Rule 440 requirements or filing procedures.

18        My testimony relies on the capital expenditure data reflected in SPS’s accounting


                                               4
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Supplemental Testimony
                                              of
                                     Michele A. Kietzman

 1        records. Other SPS personnel are responsible for regulatory compliance matters,

 2        including the preparation and filing of Rule 440 reports.

 3   Q.   In your Direct Testimony, you provided Attachments MAK-3, MAK-4, and

 4        MAK-5, which provide the capital additions in the Base Period, the Linkage

 5        Data Timeframe, and the Future Test Year. Will each project listed in those

 6        attachments have an associated 440 Notice?

 7   A.   No. It is my understanding that under Rule 440, a notice is required for transmission

 8        and distribution facilities only if the project exceeds a $1 million threshold. For

 9        generation projects, the threshold is $2 million. The projects reflected in my

10        attachments include capital additions both above and below those thresholds. Thus,

11        some projects included for recovery in this case do not have matching Rule 440

12        notices because their costs fall below the required thresholds. In addition, certain

13        projects reflected in the Future Test Year period may not yet have associated Rule

14        440 notices because those projects have not yet reached the stage at which a notice

15        would be required.




                                               5
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Supplemental Testimony
                                              of
                                     Michele A. Kietzman

 1   Q.   Attachment MAK-BR-1(m) shows the same 440 Notice number for multiple

 2        line items. Please explain why this occurs.

 3   A.   MAK-BR-1(m) and Rule 440 notices provide information at different levels of the

 4        Work Breakdown Structure (“WBS”). Attachment MAK-BR-1(m) reflects capital

 5        additions at WBS Level 2, which provides a more detailed view of the individual

 6        cost components of a project. By contrast, the Rule 440 notices report information

 7        at WBS Level 1, which corresponds to the overall project. Because a single WBS

 8        Level 1 project can include multiple WBS Level 2 components, the same Rule 440

 9        notice number may appear for multiple line items in Attachment MAK-BR-1(m).

10   Q.   Should the amounts listed in the Rule 440 notices filed during the relevant

11        period be summed and compared to the capital amounts reflected in MAK-3

12        for the base period?

13   A.   No. MAK-3 includes capital projects that do not require Rule 440 notices because

14        their costs fall below the applicable reporting thresholds. Also, Rule 440 notices

15        are reported at the WBS Level 1, while MAK-3 reflects capital additions at a more

16        detailed project-component level (WBS Level 2). As a result, a Rule 440 notice

17        might include projects and associated costs that are not yet in service or requested

18        in this case, and therefore not reflected in MAK-3.
